channel.title: Arsenii Samoilov - Program Management Insights
channel.description: Program management insights from Arsenii Samoilov, Senior Technical Program Manager.

item.title: What Good Looks Like at the Staff TPM Level
item.description: Staff TPM is not a title. It is a set of behaviors that are visible before the promotion happens and that continue to compound afterward.

item.title: Program Health Versus Project Health
item.description: A program can be on time and still be unhealthy. The difference is in what you are measuring and at what level.

item.title: Working With Legal on Technical Programs
item.description: Legal reviews that happen at the end of a program are a tax on bad planning. The TPMs who get clean launches involve legal at the right points earlier in the process.

item.title: Running a Responsible AI Governance Program
item.description: Responsible AI is not an ethics exercise. It is a program management problem: getting AI products through internal review, external audit, and regulatory scrutiny without slowing the teams building them.

item.title: What Running a Payment System Migration Taught Me
item.description: The Roku payment gateway migration to Adyen was the hardest program I have run. The lessons are specific enough to be useful beyond payments.

item.title: Influencing Without Authority at Senior Levels
item.description: Influencing a VP or a C-level sponsor without a direct reporting relationship requires a different toolkit than influencing a peer team. The stakes and the dynamics are different.

item.title: Building Institutional Knowledge as a TPM
item.description: The programs that survive turnover have their knowledge written down. The ones that don't restart from scratch every time someone leaves.

item.title: Growing From Senior to Staff TPM
item.description: The jump from senior to staff is not about doing more of the same work faster. It is about a fundamentally different relationship to scope, ambiguity, and organizational influence.

item.title: The Program Charter: What Belongs In It
item.description: A program charter is not a scope document or a project plan. It is the contract between the program and its stakeholders about what is being built, why, and how success is defined.

item.title: Running a Pilot Before Full Rollout
item.description: A pilot is not a soft launch. It is a structured experiment designed to answer specific questions before the answers become expensive to change.

item.title: Managing Technical Debt as a Program
item.description: Technical debt managed as a list of tickets goes nowhere. Technical debt managed as a program with scope, milestones, and executive visibility gets funded and resolved.

item.title: How to Scope a Multi-Year Roadmap
item.description: A multi-year roadmap is not a twelve-month plan extended. The further out the horizon, the more the document is about principles and bets, not milestones.

item.title: Onboarding a New Team Mid-Program
item.description: Adding a new team to an active program is one of the more disruptive things that can happen to a timeline. Done well, it accelerates. Done poorly, it costs more than the capacity it adds.

item.title: Security Program Management
item.description: Security programs fail not because the security requirements are wrong but because they are treated as a track separate from the engineering program. Integration is the job.

item.title: Running a Privacy Engineering Program
item.description: Privacy engineering is not a legal exercise. It is a program management problem: getting engineering teams to design for data minimization before the feature is built, not after the audit.

item.title: The Portfolio Review That Helps Leadership Decide
item.description: Most portfolio reviews are program status reports stacked on top of each other. A review that helps leadership decide something looks completely different.

item.title: Data-Driven Program Reporting
item.description: Status reporting based on vibes and verbal updates tells leadership what the team believes. Reporting anchored in data tells them what is actually happening.

item.title: Setting Up a Program Office From Scratch
item.description: A new program office is a blank sheet and a political minefield simultaneously. The first 90 days determine whether it becomes infrastructure or overhead.

item.title: Building Trust With Engineering Leads
item.description: Engineering leads extend trust to TPMs who understand the technical constraints and protect the team from noise. Everything else is secondary.

item.title: How to Handle a Missed Deadline
item.description: Missing a deadline is a recoverable event. How you handle it in the first 48 hours determines whether it stays recoverable.
